notes: Supports 500+ caterpillar species. Slow but long-lived (300+ yrs).

dormant.alt: Large bare White Oak in winter against a clear sky, showing its broad rounded crown and stout wide-spreading horizontal limbs

green.alt: Open-grown White Oak in full summer leaf: an enormous spreading crown of dense green foliage with massive low horizontal limbs (person for scale)

bloom.alt: White Oak leafing out in early May, the whole crown a haze of pale yellow-green new growth and dangling flower clusters

fall.alt: White Oak in autumn, with a broad crown of gold, tan, and russet foliage on a massive open-grown tree

maturity.years: Slow; ~20 yrs to first acorns, 50+ yrs to full size
maturity.notes: Deep taproot makes transplanting difficult, so establish from small stock and give it full sun and room.

notes: Tough urban oak that tolerates drought, clay, and pollution. Massive acorns feed wildlife.

bloom.alt: Bur oak twig with newly opening fiddle-shaped leaves and drooping yellow-green male flower clusters

green.alt: A broad-spreading bur oak in full green summer leaf on a grassy hillside

fruit.alt: Fiddle-shaped bur oak leaves with two acorns in fringed, mossy, bristly cups ('mossycup oak')

fall.alt: Bur oak savanna in autumn: spreading oaks turning yellow-gold over tawny prairie grass

dormant.alt: Massive open-grown bur oak in winter: bare, with a short stout trunk and broad low-spreading branches under light snow

maturity.years: Slow–moderate (~1–1.75 ft/yr); up to 35 yrs to first acorn crop
maturity.notes: Deep taproot demands early siting and patience; extremely long-lived once established.

notes: Named for Kentucky. White flower clusters like wisteria; a wide, spreading shape.

bloom.alt: Yellowwood in late spring: drooping branched clusters of white wisteria-like flowers hanging amid bright-green leaves made of paired leaflets along a central stalk

green.alt: Yellowwood in summer: a young whole tree with a broad rounded crown of bright-green pinnate foliage and a smooth gray trunk in a garden

fall.alt: Yellowwood in autumn: the upper canopy turned bright golden-yellow against a clear blue sky

dormant.alt: Yellowwood bare in the cold season: a large tree showing its wide-spreading leafless branches, broad vase-shaped crown, and smooth gray bark

maturity.years: Slow (~1 ft/yr); 8–10 yrs to first bloom, then flowers every 2–4 yrs
maturity.notes: Prune only in summer to avoid bleeding; often needs corrective pruning of weak forks.

notes: Spicebush swallowtail host. Mitten-shaped aromatic leaves. Colorful in fall.

bloom.alt: Sassafras in early spring: a small tree covered in clusters of tiny yellow-green flowers on bare twigs beside a pond, before full leaf-out

green.alt: Sassafras in summer: a small tree in bright yellow-green leafy foliage against a blue sky, showing the variably mitten-shaped leaves

maturity.years: Fast early (1–3 ft/yr); matures in 15–30 yrs
maturity.notes: Suckers freely into colonies; plant young since the taproot makes established trees nearly immovable.

notes: Pink flowers on bare branches in early April. Heart-shaped leaves.

bloom.alt: Eastern Redbud in full spring bloom: magenta-pink pea-like flowers covering bare branches

green.alt: Eastern Redbud in full summer leaf: a small tree of heart-shaped green leaves set one at a time along the twigs, no flowers

fall.alt: A row of mature Eastern Redbuds in mid-October: heart-shaped leaves turned gold and yellow, no flowers

dormant.alt: Eastern Redbud in winter: a leafless, flowerless whole tree coated in snow, showing its full bare branching form

maturity.years: 4–6 yrs to first flower; 15–20 yrs to mature size
maturity.notes: Short-lived but fast-growing. Plant young; it does not transplant well once established.

notes: Flowers in spring. Red berries in fall, attractive horizontal branching.

bloom.alt: Flowering Dogwood in spring bloom: four broad, petal-like pink-veined bracts with notched tips surrounding a central greenish flower cluster

green.alt: Flowering Dogwood in summer leaf: dense opposite oval green foliage on an upright small tree

fruit.alt: Flowering Dogwood fruit: a tight cluster of glossy red elongated berries on the branch

dormant.alt: Flowering Dogwood in winter: a whole snow-coated tree in a front yard showing its broad crown and tiered horizontal branching habit

maturity.years: Moderate (~1-2 ft/yr); mature in 10-15 yrs, blooms ~7-10 yrs from seed
maturity.notes: Mulch to keep roots cool and moist; give afternoon shade in hotter sites.

notes: Four-season interest: white spring flowers, June berries (edible!), fall color, smooth bark.

bloom.alt: Downy Serviceberry in early spring: clouds of white flowers with narrow strap-like petals in loose clusters, opening with bronze-tinged emerging leaves

green.alt: Downy Serviceberry in summer: arching branches of fine-toothed oval green leaves with tiny developing green berries

maturity.years: Slow to establish after transplant; fruiting in 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Establish from small stock and avoid moving once set; berries follow within a few seasons.

notes: Zebra swallowtail's only host plant. Largest native fruit in N. America, with a tropical flavor.

bloom.alt: Cluster of nodding cup-shaped maroon, purple-brown six-petaled pawpaw flowers on a bare branch with one unfurling leaf bud

green.alt: Whole multi-stemmed understory pawpaw in full bright-green summer leaf in a woodland clearing

fruit.alt: Cluster of plump oblong green 'wild banana' pawpaw fruits hanging from a branch among large tropical-looking leaves

fall.alt: Young pawpaw in October with large leaves turned clear bright golden-yellow in open woodland

dormant.alt: Slender leafless winter pawpaw twig with the distinctive fuzzy reddish-brown naked terminal bud and smaller lateral buds, against snow

maturity.years: Moderate (~2 ft/yr in sun); fruit in 3–5 yrs (grafted) to 7–8 yrs (seed)
maturity.notes: Plant two genetically distinct trees for cross-pollination; low care once established.

notes: Earliest yellow bloom, before the leaves. Spicebush swallowtail host. Red berries on females.

bloom.alt: Multi-stem Spicebush in early spring: a haze of tiny yellow flower clusters along bare leafless twigs before the leaves emerge

fruit.alt: Spicebush fruit: glossy bright-red oval berries where the leaves join a slender twig with smooth oval leaves

fall.alt: Whole Spicebush shrub in clear bright-yellow autumn foliage in a woodland

maturity.years: Slow-moderate (~1-1.5 ft/yr); 6-12 ft in ~6-8 yrs; fruit in 3-6 yrs
maturity.notes: Plant both sexes for berries on females; keep consistently moist, especially in sun.

notes: Bright magenta-purple berries in fall, a color few other garden plants have.

bloom.alt: American Beautyberry in early summer bloom: small pale-lavender flower clusters where the leaves meet a leafy green stem

green.alt: Full American Beautyberry shrub leafed out in dense green serrated foliage in a natural understory setting

fruit.alt: American Beautyberry in fall: the signature tight magenta-purple berry clusters encircling an arching stem

winter.alt: American Beautyberry in December: clusters of persistent purple berries on mostly bare brown woody stems

maturity.years: 3–5 yrs to mature 4–6 ft; berries by year 2–3
maturity.notes: Moderate-to-fast grower (1–2 ft/yr). Cut back hard in late winter for a compact form and heavier berrying on new wood.

notes: Round 'pincushion' flowers that draw many pollinators. Tolerates standing water.

bloom.alt: Buttonbush in summer bloom: a rounded multi-stem shrub studded with spherical white pincushion flower heads amid glossy green leaves

green.alt: Buttonbush in leaf: a full rounded multi-stem shrub of lush green foliage with no flowers, in a garden bed

maturity.years: Moderate–fast (~1–2 ft/yr); blooms 3–5 yrs after planting
maturity.notes: Flowers poorly in shade or dry soil, so site it in sun with constantly moist to wet soil.

notes: Interesting in all four seasons: huge white flower clusters, oak-shaped leaves, bright fall color, and peeling bark.

bloom.alt: Oakleaf Hydrangea in bloom: upright branched white flower clusters above oak-like foliage

green.alt: Oakleaf Hydrangea in late spring: a mounded shrub of large, deeply oak-lobed green leaves before bloom

fall.alt: Oakleaf Hydrangea in autumn: a whole mounded shrub turning deep burgundy-wine red on its oak-shaped leaves

winter.alt: Oakleaf Hydrangea in winter: bare multi-stemmed branches with peeling cinnamon bark

maturity.years: 3–5 yrs to mature 6–8 ft
maturity.notes: Slow-to-moderate grower. Blooms on old wood, so first flowers come quickly.

notes: Fragrant white flower spikes, arching branches, and bright red fall color. 'Henry's Garnet' is reliable.

bloom.alt: Virginia Sweetspire in bloom: long drooping cylindrical white bottlebrush flower spikes arching from a multi-stem shrub covered in bright-green oval leaves, over mulch

green.alt: Virginia Sweetspire in summer: a dense rounded leafy mound of arching stems covered in simple elliptic bright-green leaves, no flowers

fall.alt: Virginia Sweetspire in autumn: foliage turning a mix of red, burgundy, and purple among lingering green leaves, with spent grey-brown flower spikes

maturity.years: Moderate; ~1–2 ft/yr, reaching mature 3–5 ft in 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Plant in moist, slightly acidic soil in sun for the best flowering and red fall color; avoid over-fertilizing.

notes: Peeling bark gives it something to look at in winter. The wild form supports more wildlife than the dark-leaved named varieties.

bloom.alt: Ninebark in bloom: rounded white flower clusters with prominent pollen-bearing threads on arching stems, among maple-like lobed green leaves

green.alt: A full arching multi-stem ninebark shrub in summer with dense maple-like lobed green foliage

fall.alt: Ninebark in October: yellowing lobed leaves alongside clusters of dark reddish-brown dried seed capsules (the fall color is modest)

winter.alt: Ninebark in winter: bare arching stems hung with persistent dried brown seed-capsule clusters against snow

maturity.years: Fast (2+ ft/yr); full size in 3–5 years
maturity.notes: Can be cut to the ground in late winter to rejuvenate; don't prune after mid-August.

notes: Bright red berries in winter. You need both a male and a female plant for fruit (e.g., 'Jim Dandy' + 'Red Sprite').

fruit.alt: Winterberry Holly in early fall: bright red berries crowding the stems amid glossy green, finely-toothed, non-spiny holly leaves

winter.alt: Winterberry Holly in winter: a full multi-stem deciduous shrub of completely leafless gray stems densely lined with vivid red berries against a clear blue sky

maturity.years: Slow; berries begin 2–3 yrs after planting
maturity.notes: Needs a male plant within about 50 ft of the females to pollinate them; dry soil can abort fruit, so keep evenly moist.

notes: 'Gro-Low' (2 ft) makes a good groundcover for sun. Grows well on slopes.

bloom.alt: Close-up of fragrant sumac in spring: short catkin-like spikes of densely packed tiny yellow-green flowers at the branch tips, opening before the leaves fully unfurl

green.alt: A low, spreading fragrant sumac shrub in summer, a dense mass of glossy trifoliate (three-leaflet) lobed green leaves on reddish stems

maturity.years: Slow; spreads 6–10 ft wide by suckering over several years
maturity.notes: Stems root where they touch soil; excellent on dry, poor, or sloped sites.

notes: Black-blue berries for birds. Reliable, adaptable, multi-season interest.

bloom.alt: A rounded multi-stem arrowwood viburnum shrub along a lawn edge, covered with flat-topped creamy-white flower clusters above simple opposite toothed green leaves

green.alt: Arrowwood viburnum foliage: large, undivided, coarsely toothed egg-shaped leaves in pairs across from each other, with prominent straight veins; small immature flower-bud clusters at the stem tips

fruit.alt: Dense clusters of small, round, blue to blue-black berries on arrowwood viburnum, surrounded by coarsely toothed green leaves growing in pairs

fall.alt: A young arrowwood viburnum in a woodland understory with foliage turned deep red to burgundy, on a multi-stem plant against bare tree trunks

maturity.years: Moderate (~1–2 ft/yr); mature size in 7–8 yrs
maturity.notes: Blooms on old wood, so prune right after bloom; plant more than one strain for fruit.

notes: Compact, drought-proof once established. Deep taproot, so site it right the first time.

bloom.alt: New Jersey Tea in bloom: a low mounded shrub densely covered with rounded fluffy white branched flower clusters on long stalks above green foliage

green.alt: New Jersey Tea: a low compact twiggy mound of egg-shaped finely-toothed green leaves in bare soil, with a few small white flower clusters at the tips

maturity.years: Slow–moderate; mature 2–3 ft shrub in 2–3 yrs; flowers 2–5 yrs from seed
maturity.notes: Deep taproot makes transplanting nearly impossible, so site it carefully; dislikes wet or clay soil.

notes: Big broadleaf evergreen of cool, shady, acid woods, with rounded clusters of white-pink flowers in summer and a year-round screen. Leaves droop and curl tightly in hard cold. All parts are toxic if eaten.

bloom.alt: Rosebay Rhododendron in bloom: a rounded cluster of white flowers, each with yellow-green spotting on the upper lobe and long reddish-brown pollen-bearing tips, above leathery dark-green leaves in a summer woodland

green.alt: Rosebay Rhododendron in late spring: an upright young evergreen shrub with whorled rosettes of large leathery elliptical green leaves and pale new growth at the branch tips

winter.alt: Rosebay Rhododendron in a hard freeze: leaves drooping and tightly rolled into narrow downward curls (the species' cold-weather leaf-curl response) on a bare-stemmed evergreen shrub against a house wall

maturity.years: Slow; decades to mature ~10–15 ft (long juvenile period before first bloom)
maturity.notes: Needs acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist but well-drained soil in part to full shade; mulch its shallow roots and shield it from hot afternoon sun and drying winds.

notes: A reliable shade perennial with a long bloom and a slowly spreading clump.

bloom.alt: Woodland trail edged with masses of Wild Geranium in bloom: loose clusters of pink-lavender 5-petal saucer flowers above deeply palmate-lobed leaves

dormant.alt: Wild Geranium in late autumn: low persistent basal rosettes of palmate leaves among fallen leaf litter

maturity.years: Fast; 1-1.5 ft clump in 1-2 seasons; flowers by year 1-2
maturity.notes: Shear back in midsummer when foliage yellows; self-seeds to expand the colony.

notes: Blooms in spring, then dies back to the ground by summer. Pair with ferns or hostas to fill the gap when it goes dormant.

bloom.alt: Virginia Bluebells in spring: a colony of nodding sky-blue trumpet flowers (opening from pink buds) on broad oval blue-green leaves, carpeting a floodplain forest floor

maturity.years: Slow; may not bloom until 2nd–3rd yr from seed
maturity.notes: Goes fully dormant by midsummer, so interplant with later perennials; bare-root divisions establish best.

notes: Semi-evergreen mound with foamy white flower spikes. Slow groundcover for shade.

bloom.alt: Foamflower in spring: airy erect spikes of tiny white star flowers with long pollen-bearing threads giving a frothy, foamy look

maturity.years: Slow; allow 2 seasons before dividing offsets; 10–24 in. colonies over time
maturity.notes: Spreads by runners along the ground into a groundcover; cut back damaged leaves in early spring.

notes: Top early hummingbird plant. Self-sows. Drought-tolerant.

bloom.alt: Wild Columbine in spring: several nodding red-and-yellow flowers with five straight backward-pointing red spurs and protruding yellow pollen-bearing threads, on wiry stems

green.alt: Wild Columbine foliage: a mounded clump of delicate blue-green, twice-compound fan-shaped leaflets, with a few small fading red flowers still at the stem tips

maturity.years: Moderate; blooms in 2nd yr from seed; self-sows freely
maturity.notes: Cut foliage back when it deteriorates in summer; short-lived but self-sows to persist.

notes: Fragrant lavender-blue carpet in spring. Plant with Virginia bluebells.

bloom.alt: Woodland Phlox in spring: loose clusters of flat five-petal lavender-blue flowers on low stems with opposite oval leaves, on a shaded woodland floor

green.alt: Woodland Phlox foliage: a low spreading mat of opposite oval-lance green leaves on the woodland floor, no flowers

maturity.years: Moderate; blooms 2nd–3rd yr from seed; spreads 12–24 in. over 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Cut stems back after flowering to fight powdery mildew; non-aggressive spreader.

notes: A well-known prairie native. Drought-tolerant, long bloom, seed heads feed winter birds.

bloom.alt: Purple Coneflower in full bloom: purple-pink ray flowers around a dark orange cone

winter.alt: Snow on a dried winter seed head of Purple Coneflower

maturity.years: 2–3 yrs from seed; same-season bloom from plugs
maturity.notes: Seed: rosette year 1, first bloom year 2.

notes: Aromatic foliage. Give airflow to reduce powdery mildew in humid sites.

bloom.alt: Wild Bergamot in summer: ragged lavender-lilac tubular flowers in rounded pompom heads atop square stems with gray-green lance-shaped leaves

maturity.years: Fast; full 2–4 ft clump in ~2 yrs; first bloom in 2nd yr
maturity.notes: Leave stems 12–24 in. through winter for stem-nesting bees; divide every 2–3 yrs to limit mildew.

notes: Monarch host. Vibrant orange. Deep taproot, so site it right the first time.

green.alt: Butterfly Weed in spring: a young clump of upright stems with narrow, alternate, hairy lance-shaped leaves and no flowers yet

bloom.alt: Butterfly Weed in summer bloom: masses of bright-orange flat-topped flower clusters over green foliage in a meadow
bloom.credit: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Public Domain (NPS)

fruit.alt: Butterfly Weed in fruit: erect spindle-shaped seed pods splitting open to release seeds on silky white floss

dormant.alt: Butterfly Weed dormant in the cold season: a dead brown stalk topped by a spent split pod releasing silk, in a brown prairie

maturity.years: Slow; 2-3 yrs to establish and first flower
maturity.notes: Deep taproot, so do not transplant once established; site in full sun with sharp drainage.

notes: The milkweed for wet sites. Monarch caterpillars feed on it. Fragrant pink flower clusters.

bloom.alt: Swamp milkweed in bloom: a dense clump of upright stems bearing rounded, umbrella-shaped flower clusters of bright rose-pink flowers above narrow, lance-shaped leaves growing in pairs in a wet meadow

green.alt: Swamp milkweed before flowering: an upright stem with opposite pairs of narrow, smooth, lance-shaped green leaves, no flowers

fruit.alt: A tall swamp milkweed plant at a pond edge, narrow leaves and slender erect seed pods (follicles) at the crown, several beginning to split open

dormant.alt: Swamp milkweed in autumn dieback: browning dead stems bearing open split pods releasing silky-tufted seeds, no green growth

maturity.years: Medium; 3–4 ft by year 2–3; may not bloom the first year from seed
maturity.notes: Foliage is slow to emerge in spring; leave the taproot undisturbed once it sets.

notes: A favorite of hummingbirds, with tall bright scarlet flower spikes. Short-lived but self-sows in moist sites.

bloom.alt: Cardinal Flower in summer: tall erect spikes of intense scarlet-red tubular two-lipped flowers rising above a clump of lance-shaped dark-green leaves in a woodland

green.alt: Cardinal Flower before flowering: a dense streamside basal rosette of upright lance-shaped, slightly puckered bright-green leaves, no flowers

maturity.years: Reaches 4–5 ft; blooms yr 2 from seed, often yr 1 from plugs
maturity.notes: Short-lived, so separate the basal rosettes in spring to keep colonies going; never let the soil dry out.

notes: Easier than cardinal flower. Handles average moisture and more sun.

bloom.alt: Great Blue Lobelia in late summer: an erect leafy stem topped by a dense vertical spike of blue to violet-blue two-lipped tubular flowers

maturity.years: Reaches 3–4 ft; establishes in 1–2 yrs; self-seeds
maturity.notes: Self-seeds reliably and divides easily in spring; clump-forming in moist to wet soil.

notes: Tall white tubular flowers that bridge the spring-to-summer gap. 'Husker Red' has dark foliage.

bloom.alt: Foxglove Beardtongue in bloom: a tall erect stem topped with an open cluster of white tubular two-lipped foxglove-like flowers above green lance leaves
bloom.credit: D. Gordon E. Robertson, CC BY-SA 3.0

green.alt: Foxglove Beardtongue foliage: a leafy clump of smooth green lance-shaped leaves on reddish stems, no flowers (the green-leaved straight species, not a purple cultivar)

maturity.years: Rapid; full 2–4 ft clump by end of yr 1–2 from plugs
maturity.notes: Adapts quickly; low-maintenance once established in well-drained soil.

notes: Shrub-like presence. Deep taproot, long-lived. Host for several sulphur butterflies.

bloom.alt: Blue wild indigo in bloom: indigo-blue pea-like flowers above a clump of smooth blue-green trifoliate (three-leaflet) leaves

green.alt: Blue wild indigo as a bushy summer clump of smooth blue-green trifoliate leaves with small unripe green pods forming, no flowers

fruit.alt: The distinctive inflated seed pods of blue wild indigo ripened to charcoal-black, hanging amid blue-green trifoliate leaves

maturity.years: Slow; mostly below-ground years 1–3; full 3–4 ft clump by year 4–5
maturity.notes: Deep taproot makes transplanting hard, so site it carefully; the clump gets bushier each year.

notes: Short-lived (often biennial) but self-sows. One of the best-known prairie wildflowers.

bloom.alt: Black-eyed Susan in full bloom: golden-yellow daisy flowers with dark brown domed centers on coarse, hairy stems in a summer meadow

green.alt: Black-eyed Susan overwintering: a ground-level basal rosette of broad, coarse, densely hairy green leaves among leaf litter, no flowers

winter.alt: Black-eyed Susan in late autumn: several standing dried stems topped with rounded spiky dark-brown seed-head cones in a meadow of faded grasses

maturity.years: Fast; blooms the first year from early-started seed; short-lived
maturity.notes: Self-sows freely to persist; deadhead to extend bloom and avoid high-nitrogen feeding.

notes: Upright purple spike that blooms from the top down, which is unusual. Monarchs visit it often.

bloom.alt: A sunny bed filled with tall, dense, cylindrical wand-like spikes of Dense Blazing Star, tightly packed with magenta-purple feathery flowers, rising from narrow grass-like foliage

green.alt: Liatris spicata in spring emergence: clusters of narrow, pointed green leaf shoots pushing up through last season's tan dead litter; no flower spike yet

maturity.years: Medium; 1 stalk in year 1 from its bulb-like root (corm), 3–5 stalks in year 2; 3–6 ft
maturity.notes: Can flop when tall, and full sun makes sturdier stems; leave hollow stems for bee nesting.

notes: Airy fine texture, long bloom. Choose the wild form over the named variety 'Moonbeam' for wildlife.

bloom.alt: A single bright-golden-yellow daisy of Coreopsis verticillata (eight rays, small yellow center) held above a mound of fine, needle-like whorled threadleaf foliage

maturity.years: Rapid; fills a 2–3 ft clump within 2 yrs
maturity.notes: Spreads by rhizomes and self-seeds; keep soil lean to prevent flopping; divide every 2–3 yrs.

fallColor: silvery leaves around the flowers persist
notes: Penn State trials ranked it #1 for pollinator diversity. The silvery leaves around the flower heads look frosted.

bloom.alt: Short-toothed mountain mint in bloom: stem tips crowned with silvery-white frosted upper leaves around dense clusters of tiny white flowers, over broad toothed green leaves in pairs

winter.alt: Short-toothed mountain mint in November: persistent silvery-tan dried seed-head clusters standing upright on the stems, foliage browning

dormant.alt: Short-toothed mountain mint in late winter: dark weathered collapsed dried seed heads on bare stems against leaf litter, distinct from the upright autumn heads

maturity.years: Vigorous; a 3–4 ft clump in 2–3 years; spreads by rhizomes
maturity.notes: Rhizome spread is manageable. Spade around the clump each spring if you need to contain it.

notes: Tidy mounding habit (unlike floppy New England aster). Gives nectar late in the season.

bloom.alt: A low, rounded mound of aromatic aster smothered in dozens of small lavender-blue daisy flowers with yellow centers, flanked by ornamental grasses, the tidy compact habit characteristic of the species

green.alt: Vegetative summer stems of aromatic aster bearing small, stiff, oblong green leaves clasping the stem, no flowers, growing among dried prairie grasses

maturity.years: Medium; 1–3 ft mound; fills in over 2–3 yrs
maturity.notes: Spreads by runners and seed; leave dead stems standing for bee habitat.

notes: Flat-topped flower clusters (not plumed). Fuels monarch fall migration.

bloom.alt: Stiff goldenrod in bloom: a flat-topped cluster of bright-yellow flower heads atop a stiff stem with thick grayish-green clasping leaves

green.alt: A full stiff goldenrod plant: stiff upright stems densely clothed in large thick grayish-green clasping leaves, flat-topped flower buds just opening at the tops

winter.alt: Stiff goldenrod in late autumn: a stiff reddish standing stem topped with a flat-topped cluster of dried seed heads gone to fluffy white pappus, in a prairie of faded grasses

maturity.years: Medium; 3–5 ft; blooms year 2–3 from seed; a prolific self-seeder
maturity.notes: Can self-seed aggressively, so remove seed heads before they ripen; divide every 2–3 years.

notes: Tall back-of-border. Draws swallowtail butterflies. Tolerates drier soil than Hollow Joe Pye.

bloom.alt: Sweet Joe-Pye weed in bloom: a large rounded mauve-pink flower dome atop a tall stem with whorled leaves below, at a woodland edge

maturity.years: Clump-forming; 5–7 ft; blooms year 2 from plugs, full by year 3
maturity.notes: Cut back before early July for a sturdier rebloom; intolerant of dry soils.

notes: Colorful in fall and winter. Caterpillars of skipper butterflies feed on it. Don't overwater or overfertilize.

fall.alt: Full autumn clump of Little Bluestem: coppery-red stems topped with fluffy silvery-white seed heads

green.alt: Summer Little Bluestem clump in a native garden bed: upright fine-textured green foliage

bloom.alt: Little Bluestem in late-summer bloom: a slender clump with reddish stems and abundant fluffy silvery-white seed tufts

winter.alt: Little Bluestem in winter: an upright clump of deep copper-russet stems standing above bleached tan grass

dormant.alt: Little Bluestem dormant in early spring: weathered pale golden-straw foliage flattened by wind before green-up

maturity.years: 2–3 yrs to mature 2–4 ft clump
maturity.notes: Year 1 invests in roots, year 3 reaches full form.

notes: A tidy native grass. Fountain habit, fine texture. Seeds smell like buttered popcorn.

green.alt: Prairie Dropseed in summer: dense fine thread-like emerald foliage arching into neat fountain-like mounds (labeled garden specimen)

bloom.alt: Prairie Dropseed in bloom: an airy open branched flower cluster of fine tiny spikes held on thin stalks above the foliage mound

fall.alt: Prairie Dropseed in autumn: the fine-textured mounds turned golden-amber in a prairie planting

maturity.years: Slow; 2-3 ft arching clump; 3-5 yrs to look mature
maturity.notes: Does not self-seed freely, so divide rather than seed; very long-lived and drought-tolerant once established.

notes: Lawn replacement for dry shade. Soft flowing texture, no mowing needed.

green.alt: Pennsylvania Sedge as groundcover: a low, fine-bladed soft sedge colony spreading across a shaded woodland floor

maturity.years: Slow; spreads 3–8 in./yr by rhizomes; solid groundcover in 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Plant divisions 6–10 in. apart for faster fill; actively grows in cool spring and fall.

notes: Flat seed heads dangle from the stems. Self-sows aggressively, so use it in wild areas, not formal beds.

bloom.alt: Northern Sea Oats in summer: an arching stem hung with flat, bright-green, drooping oat-like spikelets, the signature 'sea oats' seed heads in fresh green form

green.alt: Northern Sea Oats in late spring: a dense upright clump of broad, flat bamboo-like green leaves

fall.alt: Northern Sea Oats in autumn: arching stems hung with flattened coppery-tan oat-like seed heads as the foliage bronzes

dormant.alt: Northern Sea Oats in deep winter: a frost-and-fog–covered standing tan clump with weathered persistent seed heads

maturity.years: Medium; 2–5 ft in 1–2 seasons; spreads readily by seed
maturity.notes: Self-seeds aggressively, so deadhead it or site it in naturalized areas; tolerates shade well.

notes: Evergreen, and named for being green at Christmas. Tough; good slope stabilizer.

green.alt: Mature Christmas Fern: upright green fronds with stocking-shaped pinnae

maturity.years: 2–4 yrs to mature 1–3 ft clump
maturity.notes: Medium growth rate; spreads slowly by thickening clumps.

notes: Big, bold fern. In spring, cinnamon-brown fronds that carry its spores rise above the green ones.

green.alt: Cinnamon Fern in summer: a vase-shaped clump of bright-green fronds divided into paired leaflets, with erect cinnamon-colored spore-bearing fronds rising from the center

fall.alt: Cinnamon Fern in autumn: fronds turned golden-yellow across a forest floor amid fall woodland color

maturity.years: Slow to establish, then rapid; a 2–6 ft clump over 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Long-lived; keep consistently moist during establishment or it may go dormant early.

notes: Delicate fan-shaped fronds on dark wiry stems. Grows in shade.

green.alt: Northern Maidenhair Fern: multiple horizontal fan-shaped frond whorls of finely divided light-green pinnules on dark wiry stalks in a shaded woodland

maturity.years: Medium-slow; spreads to a 1.5-2 ft colony over 3-5 yrs
maturity.notes: Colonizes slowly via creeping rhizomes; keep moist in full shade or summer heat browns it.

notes: Native, unlike the invasive Japanese honeysuckle. Hummingbirds visit it often, and it blooms all season.

bloom.alt: Coral Honeysuckle in bloom: clusters of long coral-red tubular flowers in rings at the stem tips, with pairs of leaves fused into disks around the stems

maturity.years: Rapid; 10-20 ft vine, blooms by year 2
maturity.notes: Flowers on new growth, so prune after flowering; avoid high-nitrogen feeding; train on a trellis.

notes: Early hummingbird vine. Climbs with tendrils. Winter foliage turns purple, which is unusual.

green.alt: Crossvine in summer: a climbing vine with opposite two-leaflet leaves and branched tendrils, glossy green foliage on bark

bloom.alt: Crossvine in spring: clusters of trumpet flowers, orange-red outside with a yellow throat, on the climbing vine

maturity.years: Fast; vigorous to 30–50 ft; covers a structure in 3–5 yrs
maturity.notes: Spreads by seed and root suckers, so pull suckers as you see them; resprouts after hard winters.

notes: Colorful in fall. 5 leaflets (not 3 like poison ivy). Sphinx moth host.

bloom.alt: Virginia Creeper in June: a branched cluster of small greenish-white flowers with protruding pollen-bearing threads and reddish buds, beside a toothed leaf of five leaflets fanning out from one point, on a vine against bark

green.alt: Virginia Creeper in spring: new palmately compound leaves with five toothed leaflets on a vine climbing tree bark

fall.alt: Virginia Creeper in autumn: a vine cloaking a tree trunk in bright scarlet five-leaflet foliage against blue sky

dormant.alt: Virginia Creeper in winter: a bare reddish woody vine clinging to a tree trunk by its adhesive disc-tipped tendrils, fully leafless

maturity.years: Rapid; vigorous to 30–50 ft; substantial cover in 2–3 yrs
maturity.notes: Its sticky pads cling for good, so keep it off painted or clean surfaces; trim to control.

notes: Edible berries (small but flavorful). Spreads by runners. Good lawn alternative.

bloom.alt: Wild Strawberry in spring: white five-petal flowers with yellow centers above a low trifoliate mat

fruit.alt: Wild Strawberry in early summer: small ripe red berries with surface seeds nestled among trifoliate toothed leaves

green.alt: Wild Strawberry in summer: a low groundcover patch of trifoliate toothed leaves spreading by reddish runners

maturity.years: Medium; a 4–9 in. mat; fills to a solid colony in 2–3 yrs by runners
maturity.notes: Runners root as they sprawl; most active in cool seasons, semi-dormant in summer heat.

notes: Yellow daisies on a low mat. Heavy spring bloom, sporadic rebloom through fall.

green.alt: Green and Gold as groundcover: a low mat of soft, hairy, oval toothed dark-green leaves with a few scattered yellow flowers

bloom.alt: Green and Gold in bloom: bright yellow flowers with five broad notched petals (a five-pointed star) held just above the leafy mat

maturity.years: Moderate–rapid; a 2-in. mat spreading 18 in.+; fills in 2–3 yrs
maturity.notes: Spreads by underground stems but is easy to control; divide to thicken stands; avoid aggressive neighbors.

fallColor: rigid spherical seed heads stand all winter
notes: Yucca-like blue-gray basal rosette under golf-ball white flower spheres on rigid 3-5 ft stalks. Deep taproot, so site it once.

bloom.alt: Whole-plant habit of Rattlesnake Master in bloom showing multiple greenish-white globose spiny flower heads on tall naked stems above sword-like basal leaves

green.alt: Rattlesnake Master in vegetative growth showing the long parallel-veined sword-like basal leaves with developing flower buds on the central stalk

winter.alt: Dried brown globose spiny Rattlesnake Master seed heads on tan stems against winter prairie grass

maturity.years: Slow to establish; first bloom typically year 2-3 from a container (3+ yrs from seed), mature 4-5 ft clump in 3-4 yrs once taproot is set
maturity.notes: Sends down a deep, starchy taproot in the first 1-2 years before flowering. Pick its permanent spot and plant young, because established crowns resent any division or transplanting.

fallColor: dried stems stand tan through winter
notes: Ranked near the top by Mt. Cuba for the variety of bees and wasps it draws. Mint-scented foliage, fine texture, spreads slowly by rhizome.

bloom.alt: Slender Mountain Mint with a flat-topped cluster of tiny purple-dotted white two-lipped flowers atop a smooth branched stem with thread-fine narrow leaves in pairs

green.alt: Upright pre-bloom Slender Mountain Mint stem in open meadow showing extremely narrow thread-like leaves in pairs on smooth, hairless branching stems

dormant.alt: Whole-bush late-winter standing skeleton of Pycnanthemum tenuifolium with grey-tan flat-topped seedhead clusters in dormant prairie grass matrix

maturity.notes: Plugs commonly bloom lightly their first summer and reach full 2-3 ft height with reliable flowering in year 2, then spread rhizomatously into small colonies within 2-3 years (more aggressive in moist, open soil).

fallColor: stout square stems persist tan into winter
notes: Opposite leaves fuse around the square stem into rain-catching 'cups' that feed birds and beneficial insects. Big, so give it space and moisture.

bloom.alt: Tall stand of Silphium perfoliatum with 6+ ft stems topped with bright yellow sunflower-like flowers and opposite leaf cups along the stems, Kitchener, ON.

green.alt: Close-up of the leaf pair on Cup Plant: two large leaves facing each other, completely fused around the square reddish stem to form a cup where they join it.

maturity.years: Fast once rooted; first bloom in year 2 from a plug (2-3 from seed), reaches mature 6-8 ft height by year 3, then bulks outward indefinitely via rhizomes and self-sown seedlings
maturity.notes: Spreads aggressively by both shallow rhizomes and prolific self-seeding, so give it a back-of-border spot with room to colonize, or deadhead before seed sets in late summer and edge the clump annually with a spade to keep it in bounds.

fallColor: often summer-dormant; cut back for fresh fall foliage
notes: Grass-like clumps with sky-blue three-petal flowers. Each lasts a single morning. Shear hard after bloom for a clean green flush.

bloom.alt: Two violet 3-petal Ohio Spiderwort flowers with bearded violet-blue threads in the center, tipped with yellow pollen-bearing parts, plus green buds

maturity.notes: Plugs occasionally bloom the first year but most flower in year 2 and reach full 2-4 ft clump size by year 2-3, then self-sow and spread by underground stems into a growing colony.

fallColor: leaves persist mottled bronze through winter
notes: Native counterpart to Asian pachysandra, with slow-spreading clumps of mottled semi-evergreen leaves with fragrant white bottlebrush blooms in early spring.

bloom.alt: Low Allegheny Spurge plant in March with several short white-and-pink bottlebrush flower spikes emerging at the base among matte blue-green mottled egg-shaped leaves on the woodland floor

green.alt: Dense groundcover mat of Allegheny Spurge in summer: coarsely toothed, broadly egg-shaped matte blue-green leaves clustered at the stem tips, forming a spreading woodland colony

dormant.alt: Overwintering Allegheny Spurge in late November: the persistent semi-evergreen leaf rosette mottled green and silvery-gray amid fallen brown autumn leaves

maturity.years: Slow-spreading; ~2-3 yrs to knit into a dense groundcover mat from plugs set 6-12 in. apart
maturity.notes: Semi-evergreen woodland groundcover. Water deeply through the first season to establish; spreads gently by rhizome (not aggressive like Japanese pachysandra) and needs little care in moist shade.

notes: Magenta-purple daisies on stout 3-6 ft stems. An important late-season nectar source for migrating monarchs. Pinch the stems back by half in June so they do not flop over.

bloom.alt: Bushy ~3 ft New England Aster clump in full bloom with masses of violet-purple daisy heads, roadside setting

green.alt: Close view of a hairy New England Aster stem, not in flower, with lance-shaped green leaves that clasp the stem

maturity.years: Plugs/divisions often bloom year 1; seed blooms year 2; full 3-6 ft clump by year 2-3
maturity.notes: Divide every 2-3 yrs to keep vigorous and prevent center die-out; pinch in early summer for shorter, bushier plants.

notes: Tallgrass-prairie dominant: 6-8 ft purple-bronze 'turkey-foot' seed heads, coppery fall, persistent winter stems. Skipper-butterfly host.

bloom.alt: Big Bluestem in flower: the 3-pronged 'turkey-foot' flower cluster with reddish-purple small flower spikes and dangling yellow pollen sacs at golden hour

maturity.years: Slow year 1 (deep root building); full 4-7 ft height and first flowering by year 2-3; long-lived clump
maturity.notes: Looks unimpressive in year 1 while its roots grow 6-10 ft deep. Burn or mow in late winter; never cut during the growing season.

fallColor: golden tan with persistent seed flags
notes: Flag-like seed spikes dangle from one side of each stem, with purple-orange pollen tips when fresh. Fine-textured, drought-tough, limestone-glade native.

bloom.alt: Close view of a Side-oats Grama flowering stem showing the one-sided row of small oat-like flower spikes dangling off a single edge of the arching wiry stem, each with bright orange-red pollen sacs and whitish feathery tips that catch pollen

green.alt: Tidy 1.5-2 ft clump of Side-oats Grama in summer green growth: fine-textured narrow blue-green blades forming an upright prairie tuft with thin flowering culms rising above

fall.alt: Golden-tan Side-oats Grama stems backlit in warm October light, the one-sided dried seed flags bleaching to straw-gold and dangling along arching wiry stems in a prairie

winter.alt: Dried tan Side-oats Grama stems rising above fresh snow, fine ice crystals coating the wiry stems with the one-sided dried seed flags still dangling along each

maturity.years: Fast to establish; flowering by year 1-2 from plug or seed, full clump in 2-3 yrs
maturity.notes: A clump-forming grass that grows in summer heat, very drought- and limestone-tolerant once established; cut back only in late winter before green-up and never shorter than ~8 in. to keep the clump vigorous.

fallColor: tan seed bristles persist into winter
notes: A grass for dry woodland edges that grows in spring and fall. Open clumps with airy bottlebrush seed heads. Skipper butterfly caterpillars feed on it.

bloom.alt: Several airy Bottlebrush Grass seed spikes in a shaded woodland: small spikes spreading widely at nearly right angles from the central stalk with long straight bristles and clear gaps between them, the bottlebrush look, on slender arching stems

green.alt: Lush summer clump of Bottlebrush Grass with arching broad medium-green leaf blades and emerging flower spikes rising above the foliage in a part-shade garden setting

maturity.years: Fast; often flowers in year 1-2 from seed
maturity.notes: Short-lived cool-season grass that persists by self-seeding (slowly, not aggressively) along woodland edges; cut back old foliage in late winter and let some seed drop to maintain the stand.

fallColor: green stems persist tan into winter
notes: Smooth dark-green cylindrical stems form fountain clumps in standing water or saturated soil. Brown-flushed flower clusters poke out mid-stem; year-round structure.

bloom.alt: Soft Rush in flower: smooth bright-green cylindrical stems with a brownish-green flower cluster bursting from the side of a stem, the leaf-like green tip continuing above it, over still water

green.alt: Dense fountain-form clump of Soft Rush growing at a pond edge: smooth bright-green leafless cylindrical stems arching outward in a rounded mound rising from the water

fall.alt: Soft Rush clump in October with the cylindrical stems fading to golden-tan and spent brown flower clusters, amid still-green autumn vegetation at a wet edge

dormant.alt: Late-January Soft Rush tussock in standing water: outer straw-tan stems collapsed and arching out around a still-green center, bare trees and overcast sky behind

maturity.years: Fast; fills to a 2-3 ft fountain clump in 1-2 yrs from a plug
maturity.notes: Wetland rush. Keep the soil consistently moist to wet (pond margin, rain garden); spreads steadily by rhizome and is easily divided every few years if it outgrows its spot.

fallColor: warty pods split to release silk
notes: Spreads fast by underground stems, so give it a contained or wild spot. Monarch caterpillars feed on it. Fragrant pink-purple flower clusters; warty pods burst open with silken seeds.

bloom.alt: Upright Common Milkweed plant showing broad oval leaves in pairs and clusters of dusty pink-mauve star-shaped flowers where the leaves meet the stem, against a soybean field
